Apple on Friday filed a blockbuster lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the company of stealing trade secrets. There are many intriguing details in the initial complaint, but one data point in particular caught my attention: the number of former Apple employees currently working at OpenAI.

More than 400 Apple employees are now working at OpenAI

According to Apple's complaint, more than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI. Apple therefore says it's 'unsurprising' that OpenAI employees have access to Apple's confidential information:

It's not surprising that more than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI, and therefore some OpenAI personnel have access to Apple's confidential and proprietary information—information they were obligated to protect. Yet OpenAI has chosen to leverage this confidential information to extract even more from Apple's current employees and trusted partners, using carefully crafted interview processes designed to elicit additional Apple secrets—while attempting to conceal its actions. The fact that OpenAI now employs a group of people who were once entrusted with Apple's trade secrets does not give OpenAI the right to use that information to fuel its own hardware ambitions.

Although Apple didn't get into specifics, according to a report from Bloomberg, numerous teams inside Apple have lost employees to OpenAI. The most recent example is OpenAI's hire of Paul Meade, who previously worked on the Apple Vision Pro and Apple smart glasses projects.

In fact, Bloomberg reported on Saturday that 'most' of OpenAI's hires from Apple came from the engineering organization led by John Ternus, who is set to take over as Apple CEO. The report also notes that OpenAI hardware lead and former Apple design chief Tang Tan had a 'tense' relationship with Ternus during his time at Apple.

The outcome of Apple's lawsuit against OpenAI remains unknown. Regardless, it's sure to be a fascinating spectacle—especially once the case enters the discovery phase. What do you think about the lawsuit? Let us know in the comments.
